back: a signal whose value varies continuously (like a microphone's voltage) rather than jumping between discrete levels.
hardware that samples a continuous voltage and converts it to a number the CPU can read. On the ESP32: `analogRead()`.
the SI unit of electric current; how many electrons flow past a point per second. See Current, Ohm's law.
the Atmel (now Microchip) 8-bit microcontroller family used in the Arduino Uno (ATmega328P).
the number of symbol changes per second on a serial line; 9600 baud ≈ 9600 bits/s. The ESP32's default debug baud is 115200.
a reusable solderless board with rows of connected sockets for prototyping circuits quickly.
a momentary switch; connect it with a pull-up or pull-down so the pin reads a defined level when unpressed.
the ability of a component (a Capacitor) to store charge, measured in farads (F).
a passive component that stores energy in an electric field; used for decoupling (smoothing power) and timing.
the periodic square wave that paces a microcontroller; a 16 MHz AVR executes close to one instruction per clock tick.
the rate of electric charge flow, measured in amps (A). Flows through a circuit.
in the ESP32 track, an object that bundles a peripheral's state (a pin) with its behavior (on/off), keeping hardware details tidy.
the manufacturer's authoritative document describing a chip's pins, registers, electrical limits, and timing. The ultimate reference for any microcontroller.
cleaning up the noisy on/off chatter a physical button produces when pressed, giving one clean edge instead of many.
a capacitor placed near an IC to absorb supply-voltage spikes and keep the chip's power stable.
a signal with only discrete levels (HIGH/LOW, 1/0), as opposed to Analog signal.
the fraction of a PWM period the output is HIGH, expressed as a %; 50 % gives the LED half brightness (on average).
Espressif's dual-core, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth-enabled SoC; the basis of the ESP32 devkit boards and this hub's C/C++ and MicroPython tracks.
the common 0 V reference for a circuit; every rail, device, and signal refers back to ground. Shared ground between boards is mandatory.
a pin you can configure as digital input or output, e.g. to read a button or drive an LED. See Pin, Register.
a two-wire serial bus (SDA + SCL) for connecting sensors and small devices; used by many breakout boards.
a pin configured as an input with an internal resistor pulling it HIGH; reading LOW then means "pressed/active". Saves an external resistor.
a diode that emits light; needs a Resistor to limit current. Long leg = anode, short leg = cathode.
the voltage that counts as HIGH vs LOW. The ESP32 is 3.3 V logic and is not 5 V tolerant — feeding it 5 V can damage it.
hardware registers exposed as ordinary memory addresses; setting a "pin" is just writing to a register. Core to the Arduino-in-C track.
the diagram language used across these tutorials to draw flowcharts and sequence diagrams.
a self-contained computer-on-a-chip: CPU, RAM, flash, and I/O on one die.
a lean reimplementation of Python 3 that runs directly on microcontrollers with a live REPL.
the Rust mode that forgoes the standard library (no OS/heap) for bare-metal targets. Core concept of the embedded Rust tutorial.
individually addressable RGB LED chips chained on a single data wire; driven in MicroPython via the `neopixel` module.
a programming construct bundling data and the functions that act on it; in C++ it's how we wrap a sensor or a pin.
the SI unit of electrical resistance.
`V = I × R`: voltage = current × resistance. The single most-used equation in electronics. See Voltage, Current, Resistance.
a GPIO configured to drive a HIGH or LOW voltage, e.g. to light an LED.
a physical or logical I/O terminal on a chip or board.
a programming variable that holds a memory address instead of a value; essential for register-level access in AVR C and for bridging to hardware in Rust.
a resistor from a signal to VCC that holds the line HIGH when nothing drives it low.
rapidly toggling a pin HIGH/LOW with a controlled Duty cycle; an LED appears a dimmer brightness (or a motor turns slower) at lower duty.
an interactive prompt where each line runs instantly; MicroPython's signature workflow.
a tiny piece of memory, often one byte, that controls or reflects hardware; e.g. `DDRB`, `PORTB` on the AVR.
how strongly a component opposes current, measured in ohms (Ω).
a passive component that resists current, protecting an LED or setting a reference level. Typical LED series value: 220 Ω.
a systems language with compile-time memory safety (ownership); well-suited to no_std embedded dev.
a method of sending data one bit at a time over a wire; the "Serial Monitor" and 9600/115200 baud links.
a four-wire high-speed serial interface for external chips and displays.
an integrated circuit that puts CPU plus peripherals (Wi-Fi, timers, ADC) together, like the ESP32.
internal hardware that counts clock cycles; powers delays, PWM, and microsecond timing.
electrical "pressure" or potential difference between two points, measured in volts.
see NeoPixel / WS2812.
the wireless networking protocol built into the ESP32; used in the HTTP server tutorial to control an LED from a browser.
